questions.question: According to 14 CFR part 1, how is an airplane defined?
questions.correct_answer: An engine-driven, fixed-wing aircraft supported in flight by the dynamic reaction of air against its wings
distractors: Any device that is used or intended to be used for flight
An aircraft that contains a GPS navigation system with a moving map display and an autopilot
A weight-shift control aircraft that is powered by an engine and supported by a parafoil
questions.explanation: The chapter states that 14 CFR part 1 defines an airplane as an engine-driven, fixed-wing aircraft that is supported in flight by the dynamic reaction of air against its wings.

reference.text: Title 14 CFR part 1 also defines airplane as an engine-driven, fixed-wing aircraft that is supported in flight by the dynamic reaction of air against its wings.

questions.question: What is required for an aircraft's airworthiness certificate to remain valid?
questions.correct_answer: The required maintenance and inspections must be kept up to date
distractors: The aircraft must pass an annual conformity inspection by the FAA
The Type Certificate Data Sheet (TCDS) must be updated annually
The aircraft must be flown at least once every 90 days
questions.explanation: The text states the airworthiness certificate remains valid as long as the required maintenance and inspections are kept up to date for the aircraft.

reference.text: This airworthiness certificate remains valid as long as the required maintenance and inspections are kept up to date for the aircraft.

questions.question: Which type of airworthiness certificate is issued for a normal, utility, or acrobatic category aircraft?
distractors: Special airworthiness certificate
Provisional airworthiness certificate
Light Sport Aircraft airworthiness certificate
questions.explanation: Standard airworthiness certificates are white and issued for normal, utility, acrobatic, commuter, or transport category aircraft.

reference.text: Standard airworthiness certificates are white, and are issued for normal, utility, acrobatic, commuter, or transport category aircraft.

questions.section: A Note About Light Sport Aircraft
questions.question: How do Light Sport Aircraft (LSA) differ from standard aircraft in terms of design criteria?
questions.correct_answer: They are designed to a consensus of standards agreed upon in the aviation industry
distractors: They are designed to FAA airworthiness standards under 14 CFR part 23
They must have individually type certificated engines and propellers
They are certified under a combination of 14 CFR parts 23, 25, 27, and 29
questions.explanation: The chapter notes that LSA are not designed according to FAA airworthiness standards, but rather to a consensus of standards agreed upon in the aviation industry, which the FAA has accepted.

reference.text: Light sport aircraft are not designed according to FAA airworthiness standards. Instead, they are designed to a consensus of standards agreed upon in the aviation industry.

questions.question: What effect does moving the center of gravity (CG) rearward have on an aircraft?
questions.correct_answer: The aircraft becomes more dynamically unstable
distractors: The aircraft becomes more stable and easier to flare
The aircraft's stall speed will significantly increase
The center of lift moves forward, increasing drag
questions.explanation: The text states that as the CG moves rearward (towards the tail), the aircraft becomes more and more dynamically unstable.

reference.text: As the CG moves rearward (towards the tail), the aircraft becomes more and more dynamically unstable.

questions.question: What are the principal structural parts of a wing?
distractors: Longerons, ribs, and bulkheads
Struts, formers, and skin
Ailerons, flaps, and trim tabs
questions.explanation: The chapter states that the principal structural parts of the wing are spars, ribs, and stringers, which are reinforced by trusses, I-beams, tubing, or other devices.

reference.text: The principal structural parts of the wing are spars, ribs, and stringers.

questions.question: What type of wing structure is used when a high-wing airplane has external braces or struts transmitting flight and landing loads to the main fuselage?
distractors: Monocoque
Full cantilever
Truss
questions.explanation: The text explains that since wing struts are usually attached halfway out on the wing, this type of wing structure is called semi-cantilever.

reference.text: Since the wing struts are usually attached approximately halfway out on the wing, this type of wing structure is called semi-cantilever.

questions.question: How does an antiservo tab function on a stabilator?
questions.correct_answer: It moves in the same direction as the trailing edge to make the stabilator less sensitive
distractors: It moves in the opposite direction of the trailing edge to decrease control pressure
It acts as a trim tab only, moving opposite to the control wheel input
It provides aerodynamic balance to reduce the physical force needed to move the controls
questions.explanation: The chapter states that the antiservo tab moves in the same direction as the trailing edge of the stabilator and helps make the stabilator less sensitive.

reference.text: The antiservo tab moves in the same direction as the trailing edge of the stabilator and helps make the stabilator less sensitive.

questions.question: How is the pitch of a propeller defined?
questions.correct_answer: The distance a propeller would travel in one revolution if turning in a solid
distractors: The angle between the propeller blade and the relative wind
The rotational speed of the propeller measured in revolutions per minute
The amount of thrust produced by the propeller at a given power setting
questions.explanation: The text defines pitch as the distance a propeller would travel in one revolution if it were turning in a solid.

reference.text: The pitch is defined as the distance a propeller would travel in one revolution if it were turning in a solid.

questions.question: Why is semimonocoque construction generally preferred over pure monocoque construction in modern aircraft?
questions.correct_answer: Monocoque construction is not highly tolerant to deformation of the surface, which can cause it to collapse easily
distractors: Monocoque construction lacks a streamlined shape and requires external bracing
Monocoque construction is highly tolerant to surface deformation
Semimonocoque uses stressed skin to support almost all loads, eliminating the need for a substructure
questions.explanation: The text explains that while monocoque construction is very strong, it is not highly tolerant to deformation of the surface and can collapse easily if dented. Semimonocoque uses a substructure to take some of the bending stress.

reference.text: Although very strong, monocoque construction is not highly tolerant to deformation of the surface. For example, an aluminum beverage can supports considerable forces at the ends of the can, but if the side of the can is deformed slightly while supporting a load, it collapses easily.

questions.question: What is a primary disadvantage of carbon fiber compared to fiberglass in aircraft construction?
questions.correct_answer: It is relatively poor in impact resistance and tends to shatter under sharp impact
distractors: It is significantly heavier and has lower bending stiffness
It has poor tensile and compressive strength
It is difficult to form into complex curved or streamlined structures
questions.explanation: The chapter notes that carbon fiber is stronger, stiffer, and lighter than fiberglass, but it is relatively poor in impact resistance; the fibers are brittle and tend to shatter under sharp impact.

reference.text: However, it is relatively poor in impact resistance; the fibers are brittle and tend to shatter under sharp impact.

questions.question: What is a major concern regarding low energy impacts on composite structures?
questions.correct_answer: They may not leave any visible sign of impact but can cause extensive hidden delaminations
distractors: They always result in visible surface crushing that is easy to detect
They cause the structure to corrode rapidly from the inside out
They immediately compromise the lightning strike protection mesh
questions.explanation: The text states that a low energy impact on a composite structure may not leave any visible sign of the impact on the surface, but underneath there may be extensive delaminations that are hidden from view.

reference.text: In a composite structure, a low energy impact, such as a bump or a tool drop, may not leave any visible sign of the impact on the surface. Underneath the impact site there may be extensive delaminations...

questions.question: At what approximate temperature do many epoxy resins begin to weaken, prompting the use of white paint on composite aircraft?
questions.explanation: The chapter states that many epoxies begin to weaken over 150 °F, and white paint on composites is often used to minimize this heat absorption issue.

reference.text: While “too hot” depends on the particular resin system chosen, many epoxies begin to weaken over 150 °F. White paint on composites is often used to minimize this issue.

questions.question: How should paint be removed from composite aircraft structures?
questions.correct_answer: By using mechanical methods such as gentle grit blasting or sanding
distractors: By using standard chemical paint strippers
By applying a specialized solvent and wiping it off with a rag
By heating the surface with a heat gun and scraping the paint
questions.explanation: The text specifies that chemical paint strippers are very harmful to composites and must not be used on them. If paint needs to be removed, only mechanical methods are allowed.

reference.text: chemical paint strippers are very harmful to composites and must not be used on them. If paint needs to be removed from composites, only mechanical methods are allowed, such as gentle grit blasting or sanding.

questions.question: How is lightning strike protection typically added to the outside layer of a carbon fiber composite skin?
questions.correct_answer: By bonding copper mesh to the skin surface
distractors: By applying a thick coat of conductive epoxy paint
By using aluminum tubing inside the composite layers
By bonding aluminum mesh to the skin surface
questions.explanation: The text states that additional electrical conductivity is added with fine metal meshes bonded to the skin surfaces, with aluminum used on fiberglass and copper on carbon fiber.

reference.text: This is done typically with fine metal meshes bonded to the skin surfaces. Aluminum and copper mesh are the two most common types, with aluminum used on fiberglass and copper on carbon fiber.

questions.question: Which category of instruments displays immediate attitude and power changes, permitting adjustments in precise increments?
distractors: Performance instruments
Navigation instruments
Primary flight display instruments
questions.explanation: The chapter states that the control instruments display immediate attitude and power changes and are calibrated to permit adjustments in precise increments.

reference.text: The control instruments display immediate attitude and power changes and are calibrated to permit adjustments in precise increments.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered a performance instrument?
distractors: Attitude indicator
Manifold pressure gauge
VOR indicator
questions.explanation: The text lists the altimeter, airspeed indicator, VSI, heading indicator, and turn-and-slip indicator as performance instruments. The attitude indicator and manifold pressure gauge are control instruments, and the VOR is a navigation instrument.

reference.text: The performance instruments indicate the aircraft’s actual performance. Performance is determined by reference to the altimeter, airspeed or vertical speed indicator (VSI), heading indicator, and turn-and-slip indicator.

questions.question: How many satellites must a GPS receiver be locked onto to calculate a three-dimensional position (latitude, longitude, and altitude)?
distractors: At least two
At least three
Six or more
questions.explanation: The chapter explains that with three satellites, a 2D position is calculated. With four or more satellites in view, the receiver can determine the user's three-dimensional position.

reference.text: With four or more satellites in view, the receiver can determine the user’s three-dimensional position (latitude, longitude, and altitude).
